disease.inheritance: Autosomal dominant — CTG trinucleotide repeat expansion in the 3' UTR of DMPK
disease.mechanism: RNA toxicity (not protein toxicity). The expanded CUG repeat in DMPK mRNA forms nuclear foci that sequester RNA-binding proteins (e.g. MBNL1) and misregulate alternative splicing, causing myotonia, muscle weakness, cardiac conduction defects, and cataracts. The toxic species is the mutant RNA, not the protein.
disease.recommended_modality: aso (antisense to degrade the toxic CUG-repeat RNA)
disease.autotac_rationale: NOT eligible (protein-level). The toxic species is the mutant DMPK mRNA (CUG-repeat foci), not the DMPK protein. A protein degrader would not address the RNA-level toxicity. The correct route is antisense oligonucleotides that degrade the toxic RNA, or splice-modulating small molecules.
disease.prevalence: ~1 in 8,000 (most common adult muscular dystrophy) — commonly cited; UNVERIFIED exact figure this session
disease.age_of_onset: Adult onset (20-40 years); congenital form in infancy (severe)
investigational: Antisense oligonucleotides targeting the CUG-repeat RNA (e.g. baliforsen/IONIS-DMPKRx — clinical)
CRISPR/Cas9 excision of the CTG repeat (preclinical)

disease.human_summary: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by a CTG repeat expansion in DMPK, whose expanded CUG-repeat mRNA forms toxic nuclear foci that disrupt RNA splicing. It causes myotonia, progressive muscle weakness, cardiac conduction defects, and cataracts. Antisense therapy targeting the toxic RNA is the leading disease-modifying approach.
